with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-f223338e: diagonal ray extension

For this task ID, the transformation continues selected diagonal strokes/rays from a compact multicolor motif toward a grid boundary, preserving all existing cells and the rest of the grid. Infer the active color(s), direction(s), and endpoint(s) from the current motif; do not indiscriminately extend every diagonal pair.

## Confirmed examples

- Demo 1 (23x8, background 5): color-2 diagonal pair at zero-based `(7,4),(8,3)` is continued up-right along `r+c=11`, adding 2 at `(6,5),(5,6),(4,7)`. Color-8 run `(9,3),(10,4)` continues down-right from `(10,4)`, adding 8 at `(11,5),(12,6),(13,7)`. The other motif cells remain unchanged.
- Demo 2 (19x28, background 7): color-9 motif at `(2,6),(2,7),(3,5),(3,8)` has two outward branches. Continue from `(3,5)` down-left, adding 9 at `(4,4),(5,3),(6,2),(7,1),(8,0)`; continue from `(3,8)` down-right, adding 9 at `(4,9),(5,10),...,(18,23)`. Other colored cells `(1,6)=2,(1,7)=5` remain unchanged.
- Accepted test (14x25, background 9): color-6 pair `(3,14),(4,13)` continues down-left from `(4,13)` to the bottom edge, adding 6 at `(5,12),(6,11),(7,10),(8,9),(9,8),(10,7),(11,6),(12,5),(13,4)`. All other cells, including motif colors 1,3,8, remain unchanged. Accepted with zero wrong attempts.

## Additional confirmed demos and accepted identity test

Three further demo pairs confirm that the same-color ray is selected by the local multicolor motif and may extend in different diagonal directions; do not infer direction from color alone:

- Demo (26x24, background 8): the local motif at rows 11–13, columns 9–11 contained 9 at `(11,10)`, 6 at `(11,11)`, 7 at `(12,10),(13,9)`, and 2 at `(12,11)`. The output continued the 7 ray from `(13,9)` down-left through `(14,8)` to `(22,0)`, preserving the motif.
- Demo (25x25, background 0): a motif at rows 13–15, columns 7–9 contained 6 at `(13,7),(14,8)`, 5 at `(14,9)`, 2 at `(15,8)`, and 3 at `(15,9)`. The output continued 6 from `(13,7)` up-left to `(6,0)`, leaving the rest unchanged.
- Demo (14x23, background 2): color 3 at `(1,11),(2,11),(3,10)` alongside 8 at `(1,12),(2,12)`; the output continued 3 from `(3,10)` down-left to `(13,0)`, preserving the source motif.

Accepted test (task-f223338e; 23x6): the input's only non-background cells were 3 at `(0,3),(1,4)`, 2 at `(1,5),(2,5)`, and 6 at `(2,4)` (zero-based). The correct output was exactly identical to the input: no continuation was added. This is an important counterexample to extending every diagonal pair/singleton automatically; the full local configuration must support an active ray. The test was accepted with zero wrong attempts.

## Cautions

This is motif-directed diagonal continuation, not broad recoloring or a universal rule to extend every diagonal pair in both directions. Use the full local multicolor geometry to identify intended ray endpoints. Preserve the background and original motif cells, extend only supported ray(s), and stop at the grid boundary. The examples support diagonal ray continuation but do not prove a universal rule for arbitrary configurations.

## Additional eight-demo follow-up and accepted test (2026-09-29)

Eight further demos in one instance reinforce that the source ray is selected by the local multicolor geometry and not by color alone. Preserve every original cell and only add the evidenced continuation(s); some motifs do not support any ray and remain unchanged.

- Demo 1 (28x20, background 6): local arrangement at rows 0–2 had 8s at `(0,8),(0,9)`, 7 at `(1,8),(2,7)`, and 4 at `(1,9),(2,10)`. Output extends 7 from `(2,7)` down-left to `(9,0)` and 4 from `(2,10)` down-right to `(11,19)`; other cells unchanged.
- Demo 2 (13x15, background 9): 6 cells `(8,12),(9,11)` continued down-left from `(9,11)` through `(12,8)`. Other motif cells 8,4,7 remain unchanged.
- Demo 3 (28x9, background 3): 9 at `(24,2),(25,1)` continued up-right from `(24,2)` through `(18,8)`. The other nearby colors 8,0,6 remain unchanged.
- Demo 4 (16x5, background 5): 9 at `(4,3),(4,4),(5,2)` continued down-left from `(5,2)` to `(7,0)`. Other nearby cells 6,3 unchanged.
- Demo 5 (8x25, background 2): 6 at `(3,2),(4,3)` continued down-right from `(4,3)` to `(7,6)`. Nearby 0,7,8 remain unchanged.
- Demo 6 (29x16, background 4): existing 5s `(26,14),(27,13),(28,12)` form an up-right diagonal; output adds 5 at `(25,15)` only, preserving nearby 1 and 6.
